primitives.name: Bayesian Bivariate Conditional Poisson
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model BCP(λ1,λ2,φ) reparameterization of Berkhout & Plug (2004) per Piancastelli et al.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ_{j,i}': 'expected goal intensity for team j in match i (dimensionless)', 'β_{0,j}': 'baseline log-intensity intercept for team j (dimensionless)', 'β_{j,Att}': 'coefficient for log attendance effect on team j (dimensionless)', 'Att_i': 'attendance at match i (people)', 'β_{j,F}': 'coefficient for foul effect on team j (dimensionless)', 'FS_{i,j}': 'fouls suffered by team j in match i (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Independence of matches, log-linear intensity specification, conditional distribution of away goals given home goals, fixed φ for correlation structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When φ → 0, model reduces to independent Poisson; when |φ| → ∞, dependence becomes deterministic.

layer2.mapping: GSE can map BCP's joint intensity model to NFL point distributions using team strength features (EPA, success rates) instead of attendance/foul covariates.
layer2.telemetry: Conditional ELPD2 difference between home→away and away→home directional models.

primitives.name: Conditional ELPD2 Directionality Diagnostic
primitives.verbatim_quote: Model selection by PSIS-LOO (and WAIC); posterior predictive checks on marginal mean/variance, goal correlation, and proportion of home losses; directionality compared via conditional ELPD2 = Σi E[log p(y_{i,2} | y_{i,1}, θ)].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ELPD_{2}': 'conditional expected log predictive density for directionality (dimensionless)', 'y_{i,1}': 'home goals in match i (dimensionless)', 'y_{i,2}': 'away goals in match i (dimensionless)', 'θ': 'model parameters (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Posterior predictive consistency, leave-one-match-out validation, directional factorization of goal dependence.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ELPD2 values are indistinguishable, model lacks directional preference; when one direction dominates, indicates asymmetric dependence.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to evaluate whether modeling home→away or away→home goal dependence yields superior predictive performance.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in ELPD2 scores between directional models.

primitives.name: PSIS-LOO Model Selection
primitives.verbatim_quote: Model selection by PSIS-LOO (and WAIC); posterior predictive checks on marginal mean/variance, goal correlation, and proportion of home losses; directionality compared via conditional ELPD2 = Σi E[log p(y_{i,2} | y_{i,1}, θ)].
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'PSIS-LOO': 'Pareto Smoothed Importance Sampling Leave-One-Out (dimensionless)', 'y_i': 'observed outcome in match i (dimensionless)', 'θ_m': 'posterior sample m (dimensionless)', 'M': 'number of posterior samples (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Posterior approximations valid, importance weights finite, model identifiability.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When PSIS-LOO diverges, model is poorly specified or overfitting occurs.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses PSIS-LOO to compare joint BCP models against independent Poisson baselines for scoreline prediction.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in PSIS-LOO scores between joint and independent models.

reasoning_traces.think:
The Bayesian bivariate conditional Poisson (BCP) model encodes goal dependence through a shared latent variable φ, which governs the correlation between home and away goal counts. Its likelihood is defined as a product of joint probability mass functions over matches. The log-linear intensity specification allows for inclusion of exogenous variables such as attendance and fouls, though these are not team-strength parameters. The model’s key innovation lies in its directional factorization: it evaluates whether modeling away goals conditional on home goals (away→home) or vice versa (home→away) provides better predictive utility. This is quantified via conditional ELPD2, which measures out-of-sample predictive accuracy for each direction. Model selection proceeds via PSIS-LOO, a robust approximation to exact leave-one-out cross-validation. These primitives enable GSE to assess and integrate joint scoreline modeling into its state-transition logic, replacing exogenous covariates with internal team strength features. The methodological framework is mathematically sound under standard Bayesian assumptions, but its reliance on fixed φ implies limited adaptability to time-varying dynamics unless extended with dynamic priors or time-series components.

reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: This model assumes symmetric information processing between teams, where the outcome of one team's performance influences the other through a shared latent factor. It does not account for strategic behavior or asymmetric knowledge, treating goal dependence as a statistical artifact rather than a decision-making process. In GSE, this translates to a static belief system that may fail under high uncertainty or adversarial conditions.
